lawyer:
Fida M. Kamal, Senior Advocate, instructed by Nurul Islam Bhuiya, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Mozaffar Hossain, Senior Advocate, instructed by A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent
parties:
Munshi Abdul Hai ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Sanjoy Kumar Shil ----- Respondent
full_judgment: The Court of appeal below further observed that the suit is bad for defect of party in the absence of the Revenue Officer; this observation is also based upon misconception of law, inasmuch as, the Revenue Officer has passed the order while performing his official works and therefore the Revenue Officer having no subsisting interest in the suit land is neither a necessary nor a proper party in the suit. The Court of appeal below further held that the defendant having informed the Court that he had transferred the suit land in favour of Foriduddin, the suit without him is not maintainable. This observation of the Court of appeal below is based upon conjectures and surmises, inasmuch as, the defendant has not appeal below failed to notice that a partition suit is filed against a co-sharer but the defendants are not co-sharers in the suit land; they have no semblance of title in the suit land. This finding is based on hypothesis. The Court of appeal below further held that the suit with lit seeking declaration of title is not legally maintainable. The Court of appeal below failed to consider that the learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence on record held that the plaintiff has been able to prove his title and possession in the suit land. The Court must have regard to all relevant allegations in the plaint and must look to the Substance of the matter and not its form. Though the plaintiff does not seek declaration of title, if the plaint as a whole is read together it will appear that the plaintiff in fact is seeking title in the suit lands and accordingly, the trial Court has declared plaintiffs title and possession in exercise of powers under Order 7 Rule 7 C.P.C. under this provision a plaintiff ought to be given such relief as he is entitled to get on the facts established upon the evidence in the case even if the plaintiff does not contain a specific prayer for the relief. The judgment of the Court of appeal below is not only based upon misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record, but the same is also based upon conjectures and surmises. He has made some observations without having no basis at all as there is no material on record in support of such observation. The Court of appeal below has made out a third case in finding about non-existence of Keshab and also in finding about non-maintainability of the suit. The Court of appeal below also did not reverse all the findings arrived at by the trial-Court and in that view of the matter; the judgment of the Court of appeal below is not a proper judgment of reversal."
